description:
At Bose Corporation, we believe sound is the most powerful force on earth — and for over 60 years, we have been a company built on innovation, excellence, and independence. Privately owned, fiercely customer-focused, and driven by our values, we continue to lead industries and transform lives through sound.

Today, Bose Corporation is entering an exciting new era. Across multiple global Business Units and Global Functions, we are shaping the future of audio technology, automotive, luxury, and premium experiences. We invite you to join us in this transformation.

Job Description

Principal Audio DSP/ML Engineer - Audio Technology

We are seeking a Principal Audio DSP / Machine Learning Applied Scientist to invent, develop, and productize advanced audio technologies. In this role, you will combine signal processing, machine learning, and systems engineering to deliver high-quality audio solutions for real-world consumer devices. You will work across the full pipeline—from algorithm research and deployment to optimized, real-time deployment on production hardware.

Bose has a strong history of combining creative thinking with cutting-edge technology in the audio domain. We are looking for candidates passionate about machine learning and audio to help us shape the next chapter in the future of Bose!

Responsibilities:

Design and develop audio signal processing and machine learning algorithms for speech and audio applications such as noise suppression, echo cancellation, beamforming, spatial audio, and audio enhancement

Apply primarily modern ML/deep learning approaches augmented by classical DSP techniques to audio and time-series data.

Investigate new modeling approaches and translate research ideas into practical, scalable solutions that will be experienced by millions of consumers.

Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Applied Mathematics , or related field.

Hands-on experience with machine learning applied to audio or time-series data .

Strong fundamentals in digital signal processing (sampling, filtering, FFTs, spectral analysis).

Experience with Python and/or MATLAB for research and prototyping.

Solid understanding of audio systems and acoustics .

Strong communication skills.

Preferred Qualifications:

MS or PhD in a relevant technical field.

Deep practical knowledge of:

Applied ML frameworks such as PyTorch/ONNX and/or TensorFlow/TFLite .

Audio DSP (sampling, filtering, FFTs, spectral analysis) using tools such as Python, Matlab and/or C/C++.

Experience with speech or audio ML tasks , such as:

Audio source separation / speech enhancement

Echo reduction

Microphone array signal processing

Strong software engineering practices (debugging, profiling, version control).

Proficiency in C and/or C++ for performance-critical systems.

Publications, patents, or demonstrated innovation in DSP or ML.

What success looks like:

You deliver robust, high-quality audio algorithms that work reliably in real-world conditions.

You balance audio quality, ML performance, and system constraints effectively.

You influence product direction through technical insight and data-driven decisions.

Your work ships as both licensed audio technology at scale .

At Bose, you're inspired to be and do your best and are rewarded for your unique talents! Our compensation is thoughtfully tailored to your skills, experience, education, and location, and goes beyond base salary. The hiring range for this position in the primary work location of Remote, California is: $216,000-$297,000.The hiring range for other Bose work locations may vary.

In addition to competitive base pay we offer rewards including bonus programs, comprehensive health and welfare benefits, a 401(k) plan, plus exclusive perks designed to support your wellbeing, and a generous employee discount where you can immerse yourself in our products and experiences. We are a proudly independent company—driven by purpose, guided by our values, and united by a belief in the power of sound. As the world leader in audio experiences, we’re creating what’s next—pushing boundaries and delivering transformative sound experiences for people everywhere. Join us and make your next career move a mic-drop. Let’s Make Waves.

title: Strategic Account Executive (New York City)
description:
Company Overview

Deepgram is bringing the world’s most natural interface, voice, to the technology we use every day. Our speech models and real-time infrastructure power AI systems that keep up with the way people actually speak. More than 5,000 organizations run conversational voice AI on Deepgram in production, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box.

The Deepgram Voice Agent Platform brings together speech-to-text, text-to-speech and speech-to-speech, with voice-native foundation models available through cloud APIs or self-hosted and on-premises deployments. Built for accuracy, low latency and cost efficiency, Deepgram makes high-quality voice experiences practical to build and run at scale. More than 650,000 developers have used Deepgram to process more than 200,000 years of audio. Every day, more of the world’s conversations with AI run on our models.

Operating Principles

Deepgram is a research company that productizes as fast as possible. Four Operating Principles shape how we think, decide, and work together:

Compress before you communicate. You think it through first, then lead with the bottom line.

Resist entropy. You question what already exists before adding more process or tools.

Solve the category. You fix recurring problems at the source, not one case at a time.

Work at the frontier. You go after problems no one has solved yet.

We look for people who already work this way, and these principles shape how we grow and evaluate our team.

AI-First by Default

We build AI that millions of people talk to, and we run the company the same way. AI is how we centralize work here, and is core to how we operate.

That means more than using the tools. We expect you to:

Build, not just use. Design your own workflows and agents, and use AI to remove whole categories of work instead of doing the same work faster.

Own the output. AI can speed up the work. It doesn’t make anyone less accountable for it. You understand, verify, and stand behind everything you share, including what an agent produces for you.

Spend the time you get back at the frontier. The capacity AI creates goes toward problems no one has solved yet.

Keep pace. Models and tools change every month, and so will your work. You adopt what’s new quickly and drop what no longer earns its place.

We judge AI by what it helps you deliver and whether you stand behind the result, not by how often you use it. In interviews, expect to walk us through a workflow you built and where you drew the line between AI and your own judgment.

Deepgram is looking for a Strategic Account Executive to drive new customers and revenue at our rapidly growing company. This individual will focus on Fortune 500 accounts across the greater New York area. While there is no requirement to work from an office, Deepgram has a local office available for those who wish to use it. We are prioritizing candidates who can regularly meet with customers in person throughout the region.

You will have the opportunity to sell a patented, world-class Voice AI platform that enables our customers to achieve things previously not possible with voice. We are looking for hungry and talented sales professionals to help us take our top-line revenue to new heights!

What You’ll Do

Own and grow a portfolio of Fortune 500 accounts across the greater New York area

Build strong relationships with customers through regular in-person meetings and strategic engagement

Self-prospect to build a strong pipeline of new logos and exceed quarterly and annual sales targets, while partnering with the Marketing, SDR, and Partner teams to generate meetings

Work closely with cross-functional teams, especially Sales Operations and Sales Engineering, to ensure sales effectiveness

Develop a deep understanding of customer needs across the STT, TTS, and Voice Agent space, as well as Deepgram’s products and competitive landscape, to clearly articulate our value proposition

Establish and maintain relationships with key stakeholders, partnering with CSMs to identify expansion opportunities and support ongoing account management

You’ll Love This Role If You

Value working with experienced leadership that has a strong track record of success

Thrive alongside high-performing cross-functional partners across GTM

Understand the importance of selling a market-validated product that delivers on its technical promise

Believe there should be no cap on your upside and want ownership of account expansion opportunities

Are passionate about what Deepgram is building and how we are changing what is possible with speech

It’s Important to Us That You Have

7–12+ years of experience in a technical, full-cycle sales role

Proven experience managing complex enterprise or strategic new-business and expansion sales cycles

Experience selling into and navigating large, complex organizations, ideally Fortune 500 accounts

Experience building your own pipeline and closing new accounts

A track record of consistently exceeding sales targets

The ability and willingness to regularly meet customers in person throughout the greater New York area

Strong written and verbal communication skills

Empathy and a unique ability to understand customer needs

Exceptional organization and follow-up skills, with the ability to manage multiple opportunities simultaneously

The ability to drive a consistent and repeatable sales process

It Would Be Great If You Had

Familiarity with Challenger or Triangle sales methodologies

Experience selling technical products to engineering, product, or other highly technical audiences

Notice : We're aware of individuals impersonating Deepgram recruiters. All legitimate Deepgram recruiting communication comes from an @ deepgram.com email address. If you've received a message claiming to be Deepgram, please forward it to careers@deepgram.com.

title: Machine Learning Engineer, CreativeFlux, AI Studios
description:
Join the AI Studios Engineering org within Prime Video and Amazon MGM Studios as a Machine Learning Engineer on CreativeFlux, the ML platform powering Nara, our AI-native content creation platform for professional animation and live action/VFX.

You will own the training and serving infrastructure that puts generative models in front of artists working on Prime Video's animated and live action productions. You'll work daily with Applied Scientists, animators, filmmakers, and storytellers, building the systems that turn new model architectures into production-grade tools artists can rely on under tight deadlines.

This role suits engineers who want their work to expand what storytelling can look like, putting new generative capabilities into the hands of the people building Prime Video's animated and live action shows.

Key job responsibilities
Design, deploy, and operate ML training and inference workloads on EKS, including GPU node groups, custom schedulers, autoscaling, resource quotas, and gang scheduling for multi-GPU jobs
Integrate generative ML models (image, video, audio) into production inference pipelines, partnering with Applied Scientists to take new architectures from research to scaled deployment

Build training and fine-tuning pipelines on EKS and SageMaker, including data preparation, distributed training, evaluation harnesses, and checkpointing strategies

Improve GPU utilization, throughput, and latency on the inference fleet through batching, quantization, model compilation, serving framework tuning, and Kubernetes-native scaling primitives (HPA, KEDA, custom controllers)

Build automated evaluation pipelines and quality metrics that catch model regressions before they reach Artists, including human-in-the-loop review where needed

Drive integrations with Digital Content Creation (DCC) tools such as Adobe Animate, After Effects, Maya, and Storyboard Pro at the points where models are surfaced to creators

Own operational health of model endpoints on EKS, including monitoring, alerting, on-call response, capacity planning, and post-incident analysis
Write clean, well-tested code and participate in design and code reviews

Stay current with generative ML, distributed training, inference optimization, and GPU efficiency techniques, and apply them to move team metrics

A day in the life
As an MLE on the AI Studios team, you'll deploy and tune generative ML models, optimizing inference pipelines, and build EKS infrastructure that empowers Scientists productionalize new model architectures. A typical day includes scaling video generation endpoints, debugging multi-GPU training pipelines, or supporting a Scientist to migrate a new image model from a research notebook to a serving fleet. You'll work with other Nara platform teams to ensure ML capabilities land cleanly in production artists workflows. You'll join team standups, model review sessions, on-call rotations, and platform-wide design reviews. You'll learn from experienced engineers and scientists to gradually take on more complex challenges over time.

About the team
We're AI Studios within Prime Video and Amazon MGM Studios, building Nara, our AI-native content creation platform. Our mission is to make Amazon a leader in AI-enabled content creation, giving creators direct control over model outputs while reducing the cost and timeline of animation and live action productions.

Our engineering team spans distributed systems engineers building scalable infrastructure, ML engineers optimizing 1P model training and inference, and full-stack engineers building creative facing agentic tools.
- 5+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
- 5+ years of programming with at least one software programming language experience
- 3+ years of machine learning, statistical modeling, data mining, and analytics techniques experience
- 5+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
- Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent

title: Manager, Strategic Market Development
description:
Overview

Some companies follow markets. This role helps define them.

Shure is hiring for a Manager, Strategic Market Development who understands the world of pro-audio. In this role, you will be dedicated to identifying and quantifying new global market opportunities by combining market insight, customer voice, and application-level expertise. You will play a critical part in helping the organization understand where growth exists, why it matters, and how to pursue it successfully by translating customer workflows, use cases, and buying dynamics into clear commercial opportunities. The position supports global visibility of customer needs, strengthens industry relationships, and improves the organization’s ability to align market opportunity, solution positioning, and sales execution across regions and teams.

Strategic Market Development is a global function that collaborates closely with Shure’s Regional Market Development teams, Global Product Management, Solutions, Marketing, and Sales leaders to convert market and application insight into scalable growth strategies, opportunity narratives, and field-ready commercial guidance.

This role can be remote within the U.S., reporting to our Niles, IL HQ office.

Responsibilities

• Serve as the voice of the customer by providing impartial, data-based analysis of global trends, workflows, and unmet needs across priority applications, end-user environments, and buying scenarios.

• Stay ahead of trends and external influences, continuously identifying and quantifying new market and application-led growth opportunities

• Translate market, customer, and application insight into clear opportunity narratives and commercially relevant guidance. Collaborate closely with multiple teams to ensure alignment between market opportunity, positioning, and execution.

• Partner with regional Market Development teams, Regional Product Managers, and sales leaders through structured engagements to activate identified opportunities, support strategic pursuit efforts, and share repeatable best practices globally.

• Establish touchpoints internally and externally to ensure cohesion and consistency across divisions and regions. Represent Shure with global professional bodies, associations, and key market ecosystems, while gathering feedback from field teams and external stakeholders to assess scalable global opportunities.

• Provide efficient access to end-user, workflow, and market information that improves field readiness, supports trials and strategic seeding, and strengthens application-specific value positioning to optimize impact and ROI.

• Research and help expand sales channels, partner ecosystems, and commercial pathways for Shure solutions, maximizing market reach and accessibility.

• Develop and share repeatable plays, messaging approaches, and partnership insights that improve opportunity pursuit and support global adoption of successful market development strategies.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Business, Marketing, Engineering, Audio, Technology, or a related field.

Minimum of 8 years of experience in strategic market development, business development, application engineering, solution selling, product marketing, or a similar role with a global focus.

Experience in the audio industry, professional technology, conferencing, collaboration, broadcast, live production, content creation, or a related field is preferred.

Strong understanding of market trends, customer workflows, use cases, and buying dynamics across regions and complex B2B environments.

Demonstrates a proactive and accountable mindset, enabling the successful completion of tasks independently with minimal supervision.

Excellent analytical skills, with the ability to gather and interpret market, customer, and application insight to identify growth opportunities and trends.

Proven ability to translate technical or application knowledge into clear commercial opportunities, practical sales guidance, and scalable growth strategies.

Strong communication skills, both verbal and written in English, with the ability to simplify complexity and effectively engage internal and external stakeholders.

Experience collaborating with cross-functional teams including product management, marketing, solutions, and regional sales organizations.

Knowledge of sales channels, partner ecosystems, and go-to-market motions, with the ability to expand and optimize commercial reach.

Familiarity with global user communities, industry associations, and customer ecosystems, and the ability to establish strong market presence and partnerships.

Willingness to travel as needed to support global market development initiatives, with a minimum expectation of 25% travel.

PAY TRANSPARENCY

Shure offers a competitive compensation structure that is reviewed annually to attract, hire, and retain the industry’s top talent. Salaries vary based on qualifications, location, experience, and expertise in each respective discipline. The range displayed on each job posting reflects the minimum and maximum salary for the opportunity. The salary for this position ranges from $109,400 to $186,000, with a midpoint target. This position may also be eligible for our incentive pay program, which varies based on individual and Company performance in the year. If your salary expectations do not align, still apply as we might be flexible on the seniority of posted positions. All positions also include a comprehensive benefits package.

WHO WE ARE

Shure’s mission is to be the most trusted audio brand worldwide – and for over a century, our Core Values have aligned us to be just that. title: Speaker Systems Engineer
description:
About Sesame

Sesame believes in a future where computers are lifelike - with the ability to see, hear, and collaborate with us in ways that feel natural and human. With this vision, we're designing a new kind of computer, focused on making voice agents part of our daily lives. Our team brings together founders from Oculus and Ubiquity6, alongside proven leaders from Meta, Google, and Apple, with deep expertise spanning hardware and software. Join us in shaping a future where computers truly come alive.

About the Role

We're building smart wearables where the speaker gets a fraction of a cubic centimeter and has to be loud at the ear and quiet to everyone around you. We're looking for a Speaker Systems Engineer to own the speaker system in our products end to end: choosing and specifying the transducers, designing the acoustic path around them in very little space, setting their limits and protection, partnering with the Audio Lead on tuning, and getting them built and tested at volume.

Responsibilities:

Own the speaker path of a shipping consumer electronics product, from transducer selection through enclosure design and factory test

Translate product-level requirements into speaker system and transducer requirements: bandwidth, level, distortion, leakage, and power budget in the volume available.

Select, specify, and qualify speakers with suppliers, including evaluation of new and unconventional transducer technologies where they fit the product better than a conventional driver.

Design and simulate the acoustic path: back volume, ports and leaks, front acoustics, open-ear leakage control, mesh and sealing, in close partnership with mechanical and industrial design.

Build and measure prototypes; characterize frequency response, distortion, maximum output, far-field leakage, and excursion and thermal limits, and turn the results into design changes and better models.

Own speaker limits and protection parameters; partner with the Audio Lead on tuning and with firmware on implementation.

Work with the audio DSP team to minimize speaker-to-mic coupling through the frame.

Qualify the speaker system for reliability: sweat and ingress, temperature and humidity, drop, mesh clogging, and drift over life.

Set up and maintain speaker measurement methods in the lab and at the factory, including golden units, limits, and end-of-line acoustic test.

Support builds and factory ramps, root-cause acoustic yield and quality issues, and drive fixes with suppliers and the CM.

Work with the cross-functional team (EE, ME, FW, PD) to trade off acoustic performance against size, cost, and power.

Required Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Acoustics, Physics, or similar.

5+ years of experience integrating speakers into consumer electronics hardware, with at least one shipped product where you owned the speaker system.

Strong grounding in electroacoustics: lumped-parameter modeling, Thiele/Small parameters, enclosure and port design, and the behavior of small drivers at their limits.

Hands-on experience specifying and qualifying miniature speakers with transducer suppliers.

Extensive experience with audio test systems (e.g., SoundCheck, Klippel, Audio Precision) and with measuring distortion, maximum SPL, and rub-and-buzz.

A record of using acoustic simulation (lumped-parameter and FEM, e.g., COMSOL) to make design decisions, checked against measured hardware.

Working knowledge of speaker tuning and protection (EQ, limiting, excursion and thermal protection) and how to partner with a DSP team on it.

Preferred Qualifications:

Masters or Ph.D. in EE, ME, Acoustics, or related disciplines.

8+ years of experience in speaker or transducer development for consumer electronics.

Experience with wearables, hearables, or other products where the speaker sits close to the ear and the acoustic volume is measured in fractions of a cubic centimeter, including open-ear designs.

Hands-on experience with a range of transducer technologies beyond conventional moving-coil drivers, and a view on where each one fits.

Transducer design experience: motor, diaphragm, and suspension design, or close work with a supplier’s design team.

Proficiency in a high-level programming language (e.g., MATLAB, Python) for measurement automation and analysis.

Familiarity with human perception of sound and psychoacoustic evaluation of speech quality and intelligibility.

Experience with factory acoustic test development and yield analysis at a contract manufacturer.

description:
About Decagon

Decagon is the leading conversational AI platform empowering every brand to deliver concierge customer experiences.

Our technology enables industry-defining enterprises like Avis Budget Group, Block’s Cash App and Square, Chime, Oura Health, and Hunter Douglas to deploy AI agents that power personalized, deeply satisfying interactions across voice, chat, email, SMS, and every other channel.

We’re building a future where customer experiences are being redefined from support tickets and hold music to faster resolutions, richer conversations, and deeper relationships. We’re an in-office company, driven by a shared commitment to excellence and velocity. Our values — Just Get It Done, Invent What Customers Want, Winner’s Mindset, and The Polymath Principle — shape how we work and grow as a team.

About the Team

The Voice Agent team builds the real-time systems that allow Decagon agents to carry natural conversations across our omnichannels (phone, web, mobile, etc). We work across speech understanding, audio streaming, synthesis quality, and the voice specific execution logic that enables timing, pacing, and responsive dialogue.

Our systems must remain accurate, responsive, and stable at scale. Voice is one of the most technically challenging surfaces in conversational AI, and our small team owns this entire capability end-to-end.

About the Role

As a Staff Software Engineer focused on Voice Agent, you will lead the architecture and evolution of Decagon’s voice platform. You will drive multi-quarter projects that improve timing, responsiveness, audio quality, and reliability across millions of interactions.

You will collaborate with Research to integrate the next generation of speech models, with Infra to push the boundaries of latency and performance, and with Product to bring new voice capabilities to customers. You will help set engineering standards for voice, mentor senior engineers, and raise the technical bar for one of Decagon’s most important surfaces.

In this role, you will

Own the architecture of Decagon’s real-time voice runtime and shape its long-term roadmap

Lead initiatives that improve speech understanding, synthesis quality, and conversational timing

Define reliability, testing, and observability standards for live voice interactions

Build frameworks that make voice systems easy to debug, measure, and iterate on

Mentor senior engineers and help expand the technical culture of the Voice group

Your background looks something like this

8+ years of engineering experience with significant technical leadership

Expertise in real-time systems, streaming pipelines, or audio-based applications

Ability to define architectural direction and lead cross-functional projects

Strong debugging skills across audio, networking, and model-driven systems

Experience mentoring engineers and influencing engineering standards

Even better if you have

Experience with speech recognition or synthesis systems

Experience with VAD, streaming protocols, or other real-time audio systems

Experience designing or maintaining LLM-driven applications

Experience optimizing performance for low-latency use cases

Compensation

$200K – $400K + Offers Equity

This range reflects the expected compensation for this role. Compensation within the range is determined based on experience, skills, and the scope of responsibilities, with flexibility for candidates who demonstrate exceptional impact.

In addition to base salary, we offer competitive equity. Final compensation may vary based on location within the United States.

Medical, Dental, and Vision benefits for you and your family

description:

From the boardroom to factory floor, we create a culture where everyone is respected and where people can be themselves. You will be part of a global laboratory where different perspectives and experiences will help you solve problems in new ways. This is where you can build a long and wide-ranging career.

Senior Acoustic Engineer – Video Conferencing

Location: Austin, Texas
Department: Engineering / Audio
Experience: 7–10 years
Employment Type: Full-time

Position Summary

We are seeking a Senior Acoustic Engineer with 7–10 years of experience in acoustic and audio system development, preferably in the video conferencing, collaboration, consumer electronics, or professional audio industry.

The successful candidate will be responsible for designing, developing, and optimizing acoustic systems for video conferencing products, including microphones, loudspeakers, acoustic echo cancellation, beamforming, sound source localization, noise reduction, and overall audio performance. This role requires strong hands-on engineering skills and the ability to work closely with hardware, software, DSP, mechanical, and product teams to deliver high-quality audio experiences.

Key Responsibilities

Design and optimize acoustic systems for video conferencing devices, including microphones, loudspeakers, and audio signal paths.

Develop and tune microphone arrays , beamforming, sound source localization (SSL), and talker detection algorithms.

Analyze and optimize acoustic echo cancellation (AEC) , noise reduction, dereverberation, automatic gain control, and other audio processing algorithms.

Perform acoustic measurements and characterize microphone and loudspeaker performance using laboratory equipment and industry-standard methodologies.

Develop acoustic test plans, measurement methodologies, and performance criteria for product development and certification.

Investigate and resolve audio quality issues such as echo, feedback, distortion, reverberation, noise, coloration, and poor speech intelligibility.

Analyze frequency response, polar patterns, directivity, SNR, THD, sensitivity, latency, and other acoustic/audio performance metrics.

Work closely with mechanical engineers on microphone and speaker placement, enclosure design, acoustic isolation, vibration coupling, and airflow/noise issues.

Collaborate with DSP/software engineers to develop, integrate, tune, and validate real-time audio processing algorithms.

Develop simulation and data-analysis tools using Python, MATLAB, or similar tools.

Conduct subjective listening tests and correlate objective acoustic measurements with perceived audio quality.

Support product bring-up, debugging, certification, and production validation.

Work with cross-functional teams to define acoustic requirements and drive issues to resolution.

Mentor junior engineers and provide technical leadership in acoustic and audio system development.

Stay current with emerging technologies in audio AI, machine learning, spatial audio, microphone arrays, and intelligent conferencing systems.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's or Master's degree in Acoustics, Electrical Engineering, Audio Engineering, Mechanical Engineering , or a related field.

7–10 years of relevant industry experience in acoustics, audio, DSP, or audio product development.

Strong understanding of acoustic fundamentals, microphone and loudspeaker characteristics, and room acoustics.

Hands-on experience with microphone arrays and audio system characterization.

Experience with audio DSP concepts and algorithms such as AEC, beamforming, noise reduction, dereverberation, AGC, and sound source localization.

Experience using acoustic measurement equipment and audio analysis tools.

Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

Proficiency with Python, MATLAB, or similar engineering/data-analysis tools .

Experience analyzing recorded audio data and developing automated audio test and analysis tools.

Strong communication and documentation skills.

Ability to work effectively across hardware, software, DSP, mechanical, and product engineering teams.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience developing video conferencing, meeting room, speakerphone, soundbar, camera, or collaboration products .

Experience with microphone-array design and optimization for far-field speech capture.

Experience with beamforming, SSL, AEC, noise suppression, dereverberation, and speech enhancement .

Experience with audio AI/ML technologies for speech enhancement, speaker/talker detection, noise classification, or intelligent audio processing.

Knowledge of ITU, Microsoft Teams, Zoom, or other conferencing audio specifications and certification requirements .

Experience with multi-channel audio, synchronized audio playback, low-latency audio systems, or networked audio such as AES67/RTP/PTP .

Experience with Linux/Android-based embedded audio systems.

Familiarity with audio interfaces such as I2S, TDM, USB Audio, and common audio codecs/ADCs.

Experience with acoustic simulation tools such as COMSOL, ANSYS, or equivalent.

Experience with automated audio testing and CI/test infrastructure.

Key Skills

Acoustics:
Room acoustics, microphone/loudspeaker characterization, frequency response, directivity, SPL, SNR, THD, reverberation, acoustic isolation

Audio DSP:
AEC, beamforming, SSL, noise suppression, dereverberation, AGC, speech enhancement, audio mixing

Video Conferencing:
Far-field voice capture, microphone arrays, echo control, speakerphone systems, meeting-room audio, audio quality optimization

Tools:
Python, MATLAB, audio analyzers, acoustic measurement systems, Linux/Android, data analysis and visualization

Engineering:
System-level debugging, experimental design, automated testing, cross-functional collaboration, technical leadership

What You Will Bring

Strong ownership of audio/acoustic performance from concept through production.

A combination of acoustic theory, hands-on measurement, DSP knowledge, and practical product-development experience .

Ability to turn complex acoustic problems into measurable engineering requirements and effective solutions.

Strong attention to audio quality and the ability to balance objective measurements with real-world user experience.

Ability to work independently while providing technical leadership to a broader engineering team.

Success in This Role

Success in this role means delivering robust, high-quality acoustic systems that provide clear, natural, and reliable speech communication in challenging meeting-room environments , while helping the organization advance its microphone, loudspeaker, DSP, and AI audio technologies.

title: Senior Quality Engineer
description:
Change people’s lives and love what you do! Cochlear develops world-leading medical devices that help people hear. As a top 100 medical device company and market-leader in implantable hearing devices, more people choose a Cochlear-branded cochlear implant system than any other. Our employees tell us that the number one reason they enjoy working for Cochlear is the opportunity to make a difference to people’s lives.

Cochlear’s mission is to help people hear and be heard. As the global leader in implantable hearing solutions, Cochlear is dedicated to helping people with moderate to profound hearing loss experience a life full of hearing. We aim to give people the best lifelong hearing experience and access to innovative future technologies. We collaborate with the industry’s best clinical, research and support networks. That’s why more people choose Cochlear than any other hearing implant company. Learn and grow with us as we tackle the most complex challenges in helping more people to hear and experience life’s opportunities.

The Opportunity

We are seeking an individual to join our fast paced as Senior Quality Engineer to ensure regulatory compliance across the Quality Management System (QMS) and products by partnering with stakeholders, in particular providing guidance and training to stakeholders to meet FDA 21 CFR Part 820 and (EN) ISO 13485 (and related standards)

The role will provide ongoing support to Production and Engineering teams when potential quality issues are identified. This role responsible to identify and implement improvements that will ensure Cochlear continues to effectively produce compliant products that satisfy customer, regulatory and business requirements, Provide Quality System & Regulatory mentoring and direction to other departments.

In this role you will be responsible for:

Ensure regulatory compliance across the Quality Management System (QMS) and products by partnering with stakeholders, providing guidance and training to stakeholders to meet FDA 21 CFR Part 820 and (EN) ISO 13485 (and related standards), EU MDR, MDSAP.

Assist in identifying, evaluating, containing, investigating and applying corrective actions for Class 3 Active Implantable Medical Devices across Manufacturing and Logistics.

Support the Non-Conformance Report (NCR) process with regular problem-solving meetings to provide direction and support for the stakeholder. Assisting stakeholders in Concession implementation within the supporting areas.

Support First Time Quality, Fast Response and Morning Market meetings.

Conduct regular Internal audit and managing External audit.

Review of QMS documents for proposed changes or product related changes.

Identify, initiate and implement improvements to QMS processes.

Produce key performance metrics and data analysis on Non-conformance reports. Ensure timely delivery of periodic reports and scheduled activities

Partner with Process Engineering and Validation teams to design Manufacturing Quality Plans that are practical and risk-based. Support MQP implementation and assess opportunity to tighten or reduce sampling.

Ensure appropriate level of training is delivered for process changes and improvements.

Position Specific Skills and Challenges

Demonstrated comprehensive understanding of complex regulatory frameworks, including ISO 9001, ISO 13485, FDA QSR (21 CFR Part 820), MDSAP, and EUMDR, with proven ability to effectively apply these standards in practical, real-world contexts.

Strong capability in analyzing processes and issues to identify gaps or risks. Proficient in managing Non-Conformance Reports (NCRs), applying risk-based methodologies and utilizing quality tools such as FMEA, root cause analysis, and statistical process control to identify, assess, and develop effective solutions for quality and compliance issues.

Skilled in developing, reviewing, and maintaining high-quality procedural and technical documentation. Passionate about documentation accuracy, consistency, and standardization.

Working knowledge of quality practices in a Class 3 regulated Medical Device manufacturing environment, including design transfer, establishing requirements, Manufacturing Quality Planning (MQP), process monitoring and a strong understanding of IQC/FOA (Incoming Quality Control/First Off Approval) processes, Risk Management and/or Change Management Process.

Preferably certified Internal auditor (ISO 13485 or ISO 9001). Highly developed auditing skills with experience conducting and supporting both internal and external audits. Proficient in accurately interpreting findings and driving corrective actions to timely and effective closure.

Highly proficient in writing precise procedural and technical documents, driven by a passion for consistency, adherence to standards, and maintaining accurate, complete documentation.

Demonstrates strong independence in managing tasks while collaborating seamlessly across teams and departments to achieve shared goals.

Excellent organizational and interpersonal skills, with the ability to effectively liaise and provide clear, constructive feedback to internal and external stakeholders regarding project issues.

Why is this role right for you?

Minimum Bachelor’s degree in Electrical / Mechanical Engineering or equivalent .

At least 6 years experiences working in Quality or manufacturing operations in regulated Medical Device industry (preferably with Class 3 devices), including a minimum of 4 years experiences working as Senior Quality Engineer.

Experience with Quality Management tools and techniques, data analysis, metrics, reporting, application of appropriate statistical methods.

Hands-on experience in managing Non-Conformance Reports (NCRs), Corrective and Preventive Actions (CAPA), concessions, product acceptance processes.

Highly developed audit capability/experience (for external or internal audit).

Direct experience in identifying, implementing, and improving Quality Management System (QMS) processes, including collaboration with New Product Introduction (NPI) and Validation teams on Manufacturing Quality Plans (MQP).

Highly developed analytical, problem-solving and reporting skills.

High proficiency in writing procedural and technical documents.

Able to work independently as well as in collaboration with other teams and departments.

Proficient in Stakeholder management; excellent organizational and interpersonal skills and capable of providing guidance/feedback to stakeholders.

Attention to details. Passion for consistency, standards, accurate and complete documentation.

Proficient in data analysis using Microsoft Excel, Power BI, or similar tools, with hands-on experience in MES, ERP, and QMS platforms.

title: Research Staff, LLMs [EMEA - Remote]
description:
Company Overview

Deepgram is bringing the world’s most natural interface, voice, to the technology we use every day. Our speech models and real-time infrastructure power AI systems that keep up with the way people actually speak. More than 5,000 organizations run conversational voice AI on Deepgram in production, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box.

The Deepgram Voice Agent Platform brings together speech-to-text, text-to-speech and speech-to-speech, with voice-native foundation models available through cloud APIs or self-hosted and on-premises deployments. Built for accuracy, low latency and cost efficiency, Deepgram makes high-quality voice experiences practical to build and run at scale. More than 650,000 developers have used Deepgram to process more than 200,000 years of audio. Every day, more of the world’s conversations with AI run on our models.

Operating Principles

Deepgram is a research company that productizes as fast as possible. Four Operating Principles shape how we think, decide, and work together:

Compress before you communicate. You think it through first, then lead with the bottom line.

Resist entropy. You question what already exists before adding more process or tools.

Solve the category. You fix recurring problems at the source, not one case at a time.

Work at the frontier. You go after problems no one has solved yet.

We look for people who already work this way, and these principles shape how we grow and evaluate our team.

AI-First by Default

We build AI that millions of people talk to, and we run the company the same way. AI is how we centralize work here, and is core to how we operate.

That means more than using the tools. We expect you to:

Build, not just use. Design your own workflows and agents, and use AI to remove whole categories of work instead of doing the same work faster.

Own the output. AI can speed up the work. It doesn’t make anyone less accountable for it. You understand, verify, and stand behind everything you share, including what an agent produces for you.

Spend the time you get back at the frontier. The capacity AI creates goes toward problems no one has solved yet.

Keep pace. Models and tools change every month, and so will your work. You adopt what’s new quickly and drop what no longer earns its place.

We judge AI by what it helps you deliver and whether you stand behind the result, not by how often you use it. In interviews, expect to walk us through a workflow you built and where you drew the line between AI and your own judgment.

The Opportunity

Voice is the most natural modality for human interaction with machines. However, current sequence modeling paradigms based on jointly scaling model and data cannot deliver voice AI capable of universal human interaction. The challenges are rooted in fundamental data problems posed by audio: real-world audio data is scarce and enormously diverse, spanning a vast space of voices, speaking styles, and acoustic conditions. Even if billions of hours of audio were accessible, its inherent high dimensionality creates computational and storage costs that make training and deployment prohibitively expensive at world scale. We believe that entirely new paradigms for audio AI are needed to overcome these challenges and make voice interaction accessible to everyone.

The Role

Deepgram is currently looking for an experienced researcher to who has worked extensively with Large Language Models (LLMS) and has a deep understanding of transformer architecture to join our Research Staff. As a Member of the Research Staff, this individual should have extensive experience working on the hard technical aspects of LLMs, such as data curation, distributed large-scale training, optimization of transformer architecture, and Reinforcement Learning (RL) training.

The Challenge

We are seeking researchers who:

See "unsolved" problems as opportunities to pioneer entirely new approaches

Can identify the one critical experiment that will validate or kill an idea in days, not months

Have the vision to scale successful proofs-of-concept 100x

Are obsessed with using AI to automate and amplify your own impact

If you find yourself energized rather than daunted by these expectations—if you're already thinking about five ideas to try while reading this—you might be the researcher we need. This role demands obsession with the problems, creativity in approach, and relentless drive toward elegant, scalable solutions. The technical challenges are immense, but the potential impact is transformative.

What You'll Do

Brainstorming and collaborating with other members of the Research Staff to define new LLM research initiatives

Broad surveying of literature, evaluating, classifying, and distilling current methods

Designing and carrying out experimental programs for LLMs

Driving transformer (LLM) training jobs successfully on distributed compute infrastructure and deploying new models into production

Documenting and presenting results and complex technical concepts clearly for a target audience

Staying up to date with the latest advances in deep learning and LLMs, with a particular eye towards their implications and applications within our products

You'll Love This Role if You

Are passionate about AI and excited about working on state of the art LLM research

Have an interest in producing and applying new science to help us develop and deploy large language models

Enjoy building from the ground up and love to create new systems.

Have strong communication skills and are able to translate complex concepts clearly

Are highly analytical and enjoy delving into detailed analyses when necessary

It's Important to Us That You Have

3+ years of experience in applied deep learning research, with a solid understanding toward the applications and implications of different neural network types, architectures, and loss mechanism

Proven experience working with large language models (LLMs) - including experience with data curation, distributed large-scale training, optimization of transformer architecture, and RL Learning

Experience with various transformer architectures (auto-regressive, sequence-to-sequence.etc)

It Would Be Great if You Had

title: Senior Mechanical Engineer
description:
About Fortell

Fortell is designing better hearing aids for life as it’s meant to be heard. Traditional hearing aids make everything louder, but they don’t do enough to help the brain separate conversation from noise. Fortell uses a custom AI chip to separate speech from noise in real time, amplifying the important speech and attenuating the noise.

The Role

We are looking for a Senior Mechanical Engineer to join our hardware team. Reporting to our Head of Hardware, you will own mechanical design from early prototypes through high-volume production, covering the hearing aid itself and everything it takes to build and test it.

You’ve designed and launched small, tightly packaged electromechanical products built from high-precision molded and machined parts with cosmetic finishes. You’ve spent time on the factory floor at overseas vendors, you know how to work with suppliers in Asia to get parts right, and you’ve shipped products at volume. You’re as comfortable 3D printing a prototype overnight as you are working through a tolerance stack-up for a production tool. You also move fast. We need mechanical engineers who are creative problem-solvers committed to making sure mechanical is never the long pole in the schedule.

We’re a lean team, so this role goes beyond design. You’ll act as a process engineer, vendor manager, and project manager as the situation demands, and you’ll jump in wherever the product needs you.

What You’ll Do

Drive mechanical design and development of Fortell’s hearing aid products, from concept and prototyping through validation and mass production.

Design extremely small, tightly packaged electromechanical assemblies, working closely with electrical, RF, and acoustic engineers to integrate PCBAs, batteries, antennas, and flex circuits into a tiny ear-worn form factor.

Design high-precision parts for injection molding, micro-injection molding, and metal injection molding (MIM), including painted and cosmetically finished parts.

Perform tolerance analysis and stack-ups to make sure designs are robust and manufacturable at volume.

Design the fixtures, jigs, assembly tooling, and test equipment that go into making a hearing aid, not just the hearing aid itself.

Rapidly prototype using 3D printing, machining, and quick-turn processes to answer questions fast and prove out ideas.

Define and run mechanical testing and reliability validation for small devices, including drop, environmental, ingress, and durability testing.

Manage overseas suppliers and contract manufacturers: drive DFM reviews, tooling kickoffs, T1/T2 trials, first article inspections, and process qualification, on-site when needed.

Act as process engineer during builds by troubleshooting yield issues, refining assembly processes, and closing the loop between design and the production line.

Own project timelines for mechanical workstreams and keep vendors, tooling, and builds on schedule.

What We’re Looking For

5+ years of mechanical engineering experience, with products designed and launched into volume production.

Experience designing small, high-precision electromechanical assemblies. Hearing aids, earbuds, wearables, or similarly miniaturized consumer or medical devices are strongly preferred.

Deep expertise in injection molding and micro-injection molding, plus hands-on experience with MIM, cosmetic finishes, and painted parts.

Strong tolerance analysis and GD&T skills.

Proven experience working directly with overseas vendors and contract manufacturers in Asia, including on-site factory work, tooling trials, and supplier management.

Experience designing fixtures, jigs, and test equipment for assembly and validation.

Hands-on prototyping skills: 3D printing, rapid iteration, and comfort at the bench.

Proficiency in 3D CAD and drawing creation (NX and SolidWorks preferred).

Nice to Have

Experience with medical device development and design controls (ISO 13485, FDA).

Familiarity with acoustic design for hearing aids, wearables, or audio products.

Location

This role is on-site at Fortell’s office in NYC (at least 3 days a week).

Travel Requirements

Up to 20% travel overall.

Participation in hardware on-sites in Minneapolis (Tuesday–Thursday every six weeks).

Occasional overseas travel to visit our vendors and partners.

Research Interns put inquiry and theory into practice. Alongside fellow doctoral candidates and some of the world’s best researchers, Research Interns learn, collaborate, and network for life. Summer Research Interns in the Audio and Acoustics Research Group work on well-defined projects that encourage open exploration and collaboration, guided by dedicated mentors. The Research Internship concludes with a final presentation open to all Microsoft employees and, ideally, results in a peer-reviewed scientific publication.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

Currently enrolled in a Doctorate Degree program in Computer Science or a related STEM field.

Other Requirements

Research Interns are expected to be physically located in their manager’s Microsoft worksite location for the duration of their internship.

title: Consultant, Acoustical
description:
Location: NEA Offices: Boston, MA; Hartford, CT; New York, NY, Portland, ME; Princeton, NJ; Westford, MA

Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. No sponsorship is available for this position.

Are you energized by solving real-world noise and vibration challenges? Do you enjoy combining field work, data analysis, modeling, and practical mitigation strategies to help clients move projects forward responsibly? Are you curious, collaborative, and motivated by work that supports healthier, more liveable communities?

If this sounds like you, or you’re curious to learn more, this role could be the perfect opportunity. Join our Environment & Health practice as our new Acoustical Consultant in and work with us to close the gap to a sustainable future.

Your new role

Ramboll is seeking a full-time Consultant to join the Air & Climate Acoustics Team. This position can be based in any of our Northeast Atlantic offices. The Northeast Atlantic region is an unbeatable place to launch your career, putting you at a crossroads of vibrant cities, coastal and forested landscapes.

As our new Consultant, you will support environmental noise and vibration assessments for clients across high-growth and essential sectors, including infrastructure, renewable energy, ports, transportation, and data centers. You will apply sound measurement, acoustical modeling, regulatory interpretation, and mitigation design skills while learning from experienced consultants in a collaborative, multidisciplinary environment.

Your key responsibilities will be:

Support environmental noise and vibration assessments, noise mitigation design, and acoustical specifications for a variety of public- and private-sector projects

Complete technical analyses using acoustical modeling tools such as CadnaA, SoundPLAN, or similar software, including evaluation of potential impacts and mitigation options

Perform sound level surveys, vibration measurements, and related field work in settings ranging from dense urban environments to remote project sites

Review and interpret local, state, provincial, and federal environmental regulations, standards, and guidance that influence project siting, design, construction, and operation

Prepare clear technical reports, figures, and client-ready deliverables that communicate findings, recommendations, and practical next steps

Your new team

You will be part of Ramboll’s Environment & Health division, joining a collaborative team that develops innovative, scientifically sound solutions to reduce pollution, support responsible development, and improve livability. As one of the world’s leading environmental and health consultancies, our bright minds are trusted by clients to help manage complex environmental, health, and social challenges.

Ramboll is a global architecture, engineering, and consultancy company. As a foundation-owned people company, founded in Denmark, we believe that the purpose of sustainable change is to create a thriving world for both nature and people. So, that’s where we start – and how we work. Our history is rooted in a clear vision of how a responsible company should act and being open and curious is a cornerstone of our culture. Ramboll in the Americas has thousands of experts working across more than 70 offices. Ramboll experts deliver innovative solutions across Environment & Health, Water, Energy, and Planning & Urban Design.

About you

From the moment you start at Ramboll, we will support your personal and professional development so that you can continue to grow with the company. While we look forward to supporting your continued learning and development, for this role we have identified some qualifications, skills, and capabilities that will set you up for success.

These include:

B.S. or M.S. in acoustics, engineering, physics, environmental science, mathematics, or a related technical discipline

2+ years of experience in acoustical consulting, environmental noise assessments, vibration assessments, or related technical work

Familiarity with acoustical measurement methods, environmental noise regulations, and modeling software such as CadnaA, SoundPLAN, or similar tools

Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate technical findings into clear recommendations for clients and project teams

Proficiency with common office tools, including Microsoft Word, Excel, Teams, Outlook, and OneNote

Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills, with attention to detail and an interest in growing within a consulting environment

title: Manager, Supplier Quality Engineering
description:
Overview

The SQE Manager leads the Juárez (JZ) SQE function to ensure timely, effective supplier quality support for plant operations, incoming quality, new product introduction, and ongoing production. This role is responsible for building a highly responsive, service-oriented, and accountable team that works cross-functionally with Operations, Plant Quality, Manufacturing Engineering, Planning, Purchasing, NPI, Global Product Management, Product Design & Development, Commodity Management, and Suppliers to drive consistent supplier performance, prevent material quality disruptions in production, accelerate supplier issue resolution, and support new product development efforts. The role requires visible leadership in the plant, strong technical judgment, and consistent supplier quality process execution. The SQE manager drives alignment between SQE team priorities and plant operational needs, with clear accountability, service expectations, and measurable results. The SQE manager also provides regional quality leadership through close collaboration with other Corporate Quality and NPI teams.

Responsibilities

Provide visible, hands-on leadership for the JZ SQE organization, with active presence on the plant floor and active participation in key operational forums.

Establish and reinforce a proactive, ownership-driven, service-oriented culture across the supplier quality engineering team.

Ensure supplier quality support is proactively embedded in plant operations and the SQE team actively and collaboratively participates in production support.

Lead resolution of supplier-related quality issues affecting production, including containment, sort/rework coordination, escalation, root cause analysis, corrective action, and recurrence prevention through the SCAR process.

Drive stronger analytical rigor in investigations, especially for complex and high-value failures, and ensure the team applies appropriate RCCA quality tools with disciplined follow-through.

Manage supplier quality support across a broad range of supply models, including component/commodity suppliers, CEM partners, and JDM suppliers.

Define and implement meaningful KPIs for SQE performance, including metrics tied to plant-relevant outcomes such as response time, containment effectiveness, recurrence prevention, and supplier issue closure effectiveness.

Drive proactive communication cadence and visibility of team activities, decisions, risks, and open actions with plant stakeholders.

Partner effectively with Plant Quality, Manufacturing Engineering, Warehouse, Planning, Purchasing, and Operations to improve execution speed, role clarity, and cross-functional trust.

Collaborate with Product Design & Development (PDD), Regional Supply Chain teams and New Product Introduction (NPI) to support plant deliverables during new product development, manufacturing and launch activities.

Maintain team accountability for responsiveness, collaboration, follow-through, and continuous improvement.

Lead organizational and process improvements that increase effectiveness, clarify responsibilities, and better align SQE support to plant needs.

Ensures that adequate staffing is in place to provide supplier quality services to existing production as well as to support new product introduction projects.

Monitors execution of appropriate processes for qualifying new suppliers, including supplier surveys, reference checks, and collecting performance data.

Facilitates the development of relationships with suppliers and maintains that relationship to ensure the consistent delivery of high-quality parts.

Ensures that the Supplier Quality processes and procedures are properly documented to ensure uniformity among all divisions and plants.

Provides ongoing coaching and development to direct reports.

Performs management duties, which include setting objectives, conducting performance reviews, and facilitating departmental and one-on-one meetings.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or related technical field.

Certification as an American Society for Quality (ASQ) Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence is strongly preferred.

title: Technical GTM Enablement Manager
description:
Company Overview

Deepgram is bringing the world’s most natural interface, voice, to the technology we use every day. Our speech models and real-time infrastructure power AI systems that keep up with the way people actually speak. More than 5,000 organizations run conversational voice AI on Deepgram in production, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box.

The Deepgram Voice Agent Platform brings together speech-to-text, text-to-speech and speech-to-speech, with voice-native foundation models available through cloud APIs or self-hosted and on-premises deployments. Built for accuracy, low latency and cost efficiency, Deepgram makes high-quality voice experiences practical to build and run at scale. More than 650,000 developers have used Deepgram to process more than 200,000 years of audio. Every day, more of the world’s conversations with AI run on our models.

Operating Principles

Deepgram is a research company that productizes as fast as possible. Four Operating Principles shape how we think, decide, and work together:

Compress before you communicate. You think it through first, then lead with the bottom line.

Resist entropy. You question what already exists before adding more process or tools.

Solve the category. You fix recurring problems at the source, not one case at a time.

Work at the frontier. You go after problems no one has solved yet.

We look for people who already work this way, and these principles shape how we grow and evaluate our team.

AI-First by Default

We build AI that millions of people talk to, and we run the company the same way. AI is how we centralize work here, and is core to how we operate.

That means more than using the tools. We expect you to:

Build, not just use. Design your own workflows and agents, and use AI to remove whole categories of work instead of doing the same work faster.

Own the output. AI can speed up the work. It doesn’t make anyone less accountable for it. You understand, verify, and stand behind everything you share, including what an agent produces for you.

Spend the time you get back at the frontier. The capacity AI creates goes toward problems no one has solved yet.

Keep pace. Models and tools change every month, and so will your work. You adopt what’s new quickly and drop what no longer earns its place.

We judge AI by what it helps you deliver and whether you stand behind the result, not by how often you use it. In interviews, expect to walk us through a workflow you built and where you drew the line between AI and your own judgment.

Opportunity

Deepgram is expanding our enablement function, and we're hiring our first Technical GTM Enablement Manager. This role is the force multiplier for the technical side of our revenue organization. You will own how our pre-sales and post-sales technical teams ramp, stay current, and prove they are ready, sitting at the intersection of Product, Applied Engineering, Customer Success, and Sales.

Our technical field teams run demos, guide architecture decisions, troubleshoot live integrations, and take customers to production. You are not here to teach them their jobs. You are here to make what our best technologists already do repeatable for everyone else, and to get new hires there faster.

This is not a training delivery role, and it is not externally facing content creation. Most of what should exist does not exist yet. You will build it.

What You'll Do

Own onboarding and ramp for technical GTM roles , designing and continuously improving a structured program that gets new hires to productivity faster and creating a consistent technical standard across teams.

Build technical field framework and playbooks , including:

Technical discovery with buyers, developers, and evaluators

POC and evaluation standards, including clear technical and business success criteria

Architecture guidance for our most common customer patterns

Technical handoffs across pre-sales and post-sales

Escalation readiness, turning what we learn from individual customer issues into reusable guidance

Build and run technical certifications , keeping it current as the platform changes rapidly underneath it.

Lead technical readiness for launches , partnering with Product and PMM so technical teams are ready before GA rather than after.

Turn subject matter expertise into scalable enablement , pulling what sits in the heads of Product, PMM, and our strongest field technologists and turning it into something repeatable.

Partner with Sales Enablement where the sale turns technical, including technical discovery, evaluation strategy, competitive differentiation, and solution positioning

Operate AI-first , building the tools, agents, and workflows that let a small enablement function serve a growing technical organization.

You'll Love This Role If You

Came up in the field and would rather fix the system than keep carrying the workaround.

Are energized by earning credibility with senior technical people, and have the background to do it.

Believe in the power of AI to transform productivity, and are eager to harness cutting-edge tools to optimize performance.

Would rather ship something useful this month than design something perfect for next quarter.

Are passionate about Deepgram's mission to redefine what's possible with speech technology.

Value clarity, accountability, and moving quickly without a lot of process or hierarchy.

It's Important to Us That You Have

5+ years in technical, customer-facing roles: solutions engineering, solutions architecture, customer success engineering, technical account management, implementation, or forward-deployed work.

Real time spent building enablement for technical teams, not just delivering it.

Hands-on fluency with APIs, SDKs, integrations, and developer workflows. You can run a live demo, read a customer's integration and see what is wrong, troubleshoot L1-style issues, and hold a genuine architecture conversation. Production code is not required. Hand-waving does not pass.

Experience building onboarding, certification, or technical development programs that people actually finished.

Demonstrated ability to get content out of subject matter experts who have no time for you, and ship anyway.

Something you have built, a tool, agent, script, or workflow, that permanently eliminated recurring work. In your application, tell us what it was, what it replaced, and what it is still doing today.

An AI-native operating model: specific workflows that structurally depend on AI, and a clear account of how you would rebuild them if those tools disappeared tomorrow.

It Would Be Great If You Had

Experience with speech recognition, TTS, voice agents, LLM orchestration, or other developer-first API products.

Experience enabling both pre-sales and post-sales technical roles, and a point of view on how they differ.

Working fluency with scripting or agent building: Python, TypeScript, workflow tools, agent frameworks, or equivalent. You don't need to be a software engineer, just dangerous enough to ship working systems.

Strong writing and narrative skills, especially for turning complex technical concepts into clear, usable field guidance.

title: Embedded Software Engineer (LDN)
description:
For over four decades, Cirrus Logic has been propelled by the top engineers in mixed-signal processing. Our rockstar team thrives on solving complex challenges with innovative end-user solutions for the world's top consumer brands. Cirrus Logic is also known for its award-winning culture, built on a foundation of inclusion and fairness, meaningful community engagement, and delivering enjoyable employee experiences at every turn. But we couldn’t do it without our extraordinary workforce – and that’s where you come in. Join our team and help us continue to make Cirrus Logic an exceptional place to grow your career!

We’re looking for an Embedded Software Engineer who thrives close to the hardware and enjoys building high-performance, reliable firmware for DSP architecture and microcontrollers (e.g., RISC V and Arm Cortex M/A). You’ll design and implement real-time embedded software, optimize compute-heavy pipelines, and collaborate with hardware and systems teams to bring products from concept to production.

This role suits someone who can move comfortably between architecture/design, low-level firmware, and performance tuning—especially where latency, throughput, power, and determinism matter.

Key Responsibilities:

Design, implement, and maintain embedded firmware for DSP cores and MCUs (RISC V and/or Arm).

Build and optimize real-time signal-processing pipelines (fixed-point and/or floating-point), potentially including FFTs, filters, modulation/demodulation, codecs, feature extraction, or control loops.

Develop firmware using a mix of C/C++ (and selective assembly where appropriate), with strong focus on performance, memory, and power optimization.

Work with SoC/board peripherals: DMA, timers, SPI, I²C, UART, I²S/TDM, PWM, GPIO, and relevant bus fabrics.

Bring up new hardware: boot flows, clocks, memory maps, interrupt vectors, peripheral init, and early validation.

Implement and debug drivers and RTOS components (e.g., Zephyr or equivalent), including task scheduling, synchronization primitives, and ISR design.

Develop test strategies: unit tests, hardware-in-the-loop tests, test automation, and manufacturing/production diagnostics.

Use debugging/profiling tools: JTAG/SWD, logic analyzers, oscilloscopes, trace (ETM/ITM), and cycle-accurate profiling when available.

Collaborate cross-functionally with hardware, FPGA/ASIC, systems, and application teams to define requirements and interfaces.

Contribute documentation: architecture notes, interface specs, timing budgets, work packages, and bring-up guides.

Participate in code reviews and help establish best practices for embedded quality, safety, and maintainability.

Required Skills and Qualifications:

Strong professional experience developing embedded firmware in C/C++ for MCUs and/or DSPs.

Hands-on experience with RISC V and/or Arm architecture (Cortex M/A), including interrupts, memory, caches, and performance characteristics.

Solid understanding of embedded software fundamentals:

register-level programming, memory-mapped I/O

concurrency (ISRs, RTOS tasks), race conditions, timing determinism

fixed-point arithmetic, numerical precision, and overflow/underflow management

Proven ability to optimize firmware: cycle counting, memory layout, DMA usage, cache behavior, minimizing latency and jitter.

Comfortable with toolchains and build systems:

GCC/LLVM-based toolchains, cross-compilation

CMake/Make, Meson, linker scripts, map files

Strong debugging skills with hardware and firmware:

JTAG/SWD debugging

root-cause analysis of timing and performance issues

Source control expertise (Git) and disciplined engineering practices (code reviews, CI).

Preferred Skills and Qualifications:

Languages: C, C++, (optional) assembly, Python for test tooling/scripts

Architectures: RISC V, Arm Cortex M/A, DSP cores

RTOS/OS: Zephyr, embedded Linux (optional)

Tools: JTAG/SWD debuggers, GDB, OpenOCD/J-Link, logic analyzer, oscilloscope, trace tools

Practices: profiling, timing analysis, unit/integration testing, CI/CD for embedded

Experience with common DSP libraries/techniques (e.g., CMSIS-DSP, vendor DSP libs) and SIMD/vector optimization patterns.

Experience with Zephyr, or embedded Linux on Arm.

Familiarity with bootloaders, secure boot, OTA update mechanisms, and field diagnostics.

Understanding of digital communications, or audio, processing domains.

Exposure to safety/security standards (e.g., MISRA C/C++, IEC 61508, ISO 26262)

This Newbury or London based role is a hybrid remote position and will follow a 2 day in-office work schedule, with in-office days based on business needs and team preference. You must be based within commutable distance of the work location listed on the job posting, or willing to relocate prior to beginning employment with Cirrus Logic.
